title: Quantitative analysis of myofiber type composition in human and mouse skeletal muscles
author: Abbassi-Daloii, el Abdellaoui, et al.
materials: Myosin heavy chain type I antibody
Myosin heavy chain type IIA antibody
Myosin heavy chain Type IIB antibody
ROIs filtered based on segmentation certainty.ii.0.
ROIs included after filtering based on CSA.iv.

steps.title: Pool dataset and read ROIs
steps.instruction: Load all sample data into R using the provided R Markdown file (RStudio v1.3.959, R v4.0.2). Run the “readDataset” code chunk to pool the data from all samples into a single table.

substeps.instruction: Run the “readDataset” R code chunk.

steps.title: Filter by segmentation certainty
steps.instruction: Use the laminin‑segmentation metrics to discard non‑myofiber ROIs. Plot density distributions for Mean and Mean_boundary, set percentile cut‑offs, and apply the filter.

substeps.instruction: Run “Filt1_segmentationMetrics_denPlot” to draw density plots for the Mean and Mean_boundary measurements (Mean = laminin intensity inside the object, lower is better; Mean_boundary = laminin intensity on the boundary, higher is better).
From the density plots define thresholds; in the example dataset of 369,073 ROIs the top and bottom 5th percentiles were excluded.
Run “Filt1_segmentationMetrics_filtering” to apply the thresholds to Mean and Mean_boundary. (StdDev_boundary is not used in this example.)

steps.title: Filter by cross‑sectional area
steps.instruction: Remove ROIs with implausibly large or small cross‑sectional area (CSA) to eliminate merged fibers or non‑myofiber objects.

substeps.instruction: Run “Filt2_CSA_denPlot” to generate a density plot of CSA (μm²) for the whole dataset (including ROIs already filtered by segmentation certainty).
Define CSA thresholds based on the plot; for the example dataset include ROIs between the 10th and 99th percentiles (right‑skewed distribution may require asymmetric cut‑offs).
Run “Filt2_CSA_filtering” to apply the CSA filter. Apply per muscle group if CSA distributions differ across groups.

steps.title: Filter by circularity
steps.instruction: Exclude elongated or longitudinally sectioned objects by applying a circularity threshold.

substeps.instruction: Run “Filt3_circularity_denPlot” to draw a density plot of circularity (range 0–1) for all ROIs (including those filtered in previous steps).
Set the threshold to retain ROIs with Circularity greater than the 1st percentile of the distribution.
Run “Filt3_circularity_filtering” to apply the circularity filter.

steps.title: Visualize filtering thresholds
steps.instruction: Create visual checks after each filtering step to confirm that thresholds are appropriate.

substeps.instruction: Run “save_visualizationInput” to write a tab‑delimited file (named with a “_Filt” extension) that contains the ROI table plus columns indicating inclusion (1) or exclusion (0) for each filtering step and an aggregated column (0, 0.4, 0.7, 1).
Open Fiji (ImageJ).
Run the macro “6.Visual_Check_Filtering.ijm”, providing the directory of the original TIFF images and the ROI subdirectory.
The macro generates a JPEG file for each sample ending with “_check4” that visualizes which ROIs were removed at each step.

steps.title: Select representative replicate per sample
steps.instruction: Choose one tissue section per sample for downstream analysis, preferring the section with the highest number of retained myofibers and at least 100 myofibers.

substeps.instruction: Count the number of myofibers remaining after all filtering steps for each section.
Select the section with the greatest count, ensuring it contains ≥100 myofibers.

steps.title: Scale and transform MFI values
steps.instruction: Normalize the mean fluorescence intensity (MFI) of the three MyHC isoforms for each myofiber without centering.

substeps.instruction: Run the “ScalingAndTransformation” R code chunk to scale each isoform’s MFI per sample (no centering).

steps.title: Cluster myofibers with mean‑shift
steps.instruction: Group myofibers into type clusters using a density‑based mean‑shift algorithm.

substeps.instruction: Apply a natural‑log transformation to the scaled MFI values (performed within the clustering chunk).
Run the “clustering” R code chunk, which uses the LPCM package (v0.46‑7) to perform mean‑shift clustering.
Select a bandwidth (h) between 0.01 and 0.05; test values to find the optimum that yields 3–8 biologically plausible clusters.

steps.title: Refine clusters and generate visualizations
steps.instruction: Post‑process clustering results to remove spurious clusters and create plots for interpretation.

substeps.instruction: Discard any cluster that contains less than approximately 2 % of the total myofibers.
Draw boxplots of the MFI values for each retained cluster (example shown in Figure 13).
Generate a spatial map of cluster assignments per myofiber using the “6.Visual_Check_Filtering.ijm” macro or equivalent image‑editing step (example in Figure 14).

steps.title: Calculate cluster proportions
steps.instruction: Quantify the proportion of myofibers belonging to each retained cluster for every sample.

substeps.instruction: Compute the percentage of myofibers in each cluster per sample using the filtered ROI table.
Use these proportions for downstream statistical comparisons of myofiber type composition between experimental groups.
